From 316fb1b3169efb081d2db910cbbfef445afa03b9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: robbieko <robbieko@synology.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 18:18:15 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix incorrect return value after changing leaf in
 lookup_extent_data_ref()

After commit 1618aa3c2e01 ("btrfs: simplify return variables in
lookup_extent_data_ref()"), the err and ret variables were merged into
a single ret variable. However, when btrfs_next_leaf() returns 0
(success), ret is overwritten from -ENOENT to 0. If the first key in
the next leaf does not match (different objectid or type), the function
returns 0 instead of -ENOENT, making the caller believe the lookup
succeeded when it did not. This can lead to operations on the wrong
extent tree item, potentially causing extent tree corruption.

Fix this by returning -ENOENT directly when the key does not match,
instead of relying on the ret variable.

Fixes: 1618aa3c2e01 ("btrfs: simplify return variables in lookup_extent_data_ref()")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org # 6.12+
Reviewed-by: Filipe Manana <fdmanana@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: robbieko <robbieko@synology.com>
Signed-off-by: Filipe Manana <fdmanana@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c b/fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c
index 85ee5c79759d..098e64106d02 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c
@@ -495,7 +495,7 @@ static noinline int lookup_extent_data_ref(struct btrfs_trans_handle *trans,
 		btrfs_item_key_to_cpu(leaf, &key, path->slots[0]);
 		if (key.objectid != bytenr ||
 		    key.type != BTRFS_EXTENT_DATA_REF_KEY)
-			return ret;
+			return -ENOENT;
 
 		ref = btrfs_item_ptr(leaf, path->slots[0],
 				     struct btrfs_extent_data_ref);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File Modified: `fs/btrfs/extent-tree.c`

- **Change in function `lookup_extent_data_ref()`**:  
  At line 498, the return statement was modified. Previously, when the first key in the next leaf did not match the expected object ID or type, the function returned `ret`, which at that point had been overwritten to `0` (success) by the preceding `btrfs_next_leaf()` call. The patch changes this to return `-ENOENT` directly, ensuring an appropriate error code is returned when the lookup fails after moving to a new leaf.

### Relationship Between Modifications

This is a single-file, single-line change. The fix corrects a logic error introduced in commit 1618aa3c2e01, which merged two return variables (`err` and `ret`) into one. The merging caused `ret` to be incorrectly zeroed when `btrfs_next_leaf()` succeeded, leading to a false positive return (0) when the subsequent key check failed. The patch restores the intended behavior: returning `-ENOENT` when the key in the next leaf does not match the sought extent data reference, preventing potential extent tree corruption from incorrect caller assumptions.
